Taking your note's two options, the better fit is the second: Austin's account of law rests on an anachronistic model of a legal system. His command theory, with a determinate sovereign habitually obeyed and law as the sovereign's commands backed by sanctions, was modelled on a simple historical type of system. It doesn't fit modern legal systems, which have complex, power-conferring and constitutional rules. The first option is weaker because Austin separated what law is from what it ought to be, but he didn't deny any link between law and morality. I'm choosing between your two options and can't confirm the source of the phrase myself.

CONFIDENCE: 60
